_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 24 (Rebekah's betrothal — 67 verses, longest chapter so far). Saadia-specific moves: v.2,9 'אום בידך אלי' עהדי' = 'place your hand under my covenant' (Saadia rationalizes the Hebrew euphemism 'תחת ירכי' — 'under my thigh' = circumcision/oath — by substituting 'covenant'); v.7,40 'מלכה' = 'His angel' (intermediary, not God acting directly); v.62 הנגב=אלקבלה (qibla, consistent throughout); v.63 'יצלי' = 'to pray' (Saadia's gloss for לשוח — 'to meditate/walk'); v.27 'טריק מסתקים' = 'a straight path' (renders דרך אמת literally — 'a true/straight path').

translations.1: And Abraham had grown old, advanced in years; and God had blessed him in everything.
translations.2: And Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his household, who had charge of all that he had: 'Place your hand under my covenant.
translations.3: And I shall make you swear by God, the Lord of the heavens and the earth, that you shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I dwell;
translations.4: rather to my land, and to my birthplace, you shall go; and you shall take a wife for my son, for Isaac.'
translations.5: And the servant said to him: 'Perhaps the woman will not consent to follow me to this land. Shall I return your son to the land from which you came forth?'
translations.6: Abraham said to him: 'Beware of returning my son thither.
translations.7: God, the God of the heavens, who chose me from my father's house and from the land of my birth, and who spoke to me, and swore to me, saying, "To your offspring shall I give this land" — He shall send His angel before you; and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
translations.8: And if the woman shall not consent to follow you, you shall be free of this my oath — only my son, do not return him thither.'
translations.9: Then the servant placed his hand under his master Abraham's covenant, and swore to him concerning this matter.
translations.10: Then the servant took ten camels of his master's camels, and went; and every good thing of his master's was in his hand. And he arose and went to Aram-Naharaim, to the town of Nahor.
translations.11: And he made the camels kneel outside the town, by the well of water, at the time of evening — the time when the women come forth to draw.
translations.12: And he said: 'O God, God of my master Abraham, grant me success before me today; and show kindness in this to my master Abraham.
translations.13: Behold, I am standing by the spring of water; and the daughters of the dwellers of the town shall come forth to draw water.
translations.14: And let it be that the maiden to whom I say, "Lower your jar that I may drink," and she says, "Drink, and your camels too I shall water" — her have You destined for Your servant Isaac; and by this shall I know that You have shown kindness to my master.'
translations.15: And he had not yet finished his speech — and behold, Rebekah came forth — she whom Bethuel, son of Milkah the wife of Nahor the brother of Abraham, had begotten; and her jar was upon her shoulder.
translations.16: And the maiden was very beautiful in appearance — a virgin; and no man had known her. And she went down to the spring, and filled her jar, and came up.
translations.17: And the servant ran to meet her, and said: 'Let me drink a little water from your jar.'
translations.18: And she said: 'Drink, my lord.' And she hastened, and let down her jar upon her hand, and gave him to drink.
translations.19: And when she had finished giving him to drink, she said also: 'I shall draw for your camels as well, until they finish their drink.'
translations.20: And she hastened, and emptied her jar into the trough; and she ran again to the well to draw, until she had drawn for all his camels.
translations.21: And the man was watching her, holding back — to know whether God had made his way succeed, or not.
translations.22: And when the camels had finished their drink, the man took a gold nose-ring of half a shekel in weight, and gave it to her; and he placed two bracelets upon her hands, ten gold shekels in weight.
translations.23: After he had said to her: 'Tell me — whose daughter are you? Is there in your father's house room for us to lodge?'
translations.24: And she said to him: 'I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milkah whom she bore to Nahor.'
translations.25: Then she said: 'There is much straw and fodder with us — and also a place for lodging.'
translations.26: Then the man bowed down, and prostrated himself before God.
translations.27: And he said: 'Blessed be God, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken His kindness and His grace from my master; and who has led me on a straight path, to the house of my master's brother.'
translations.28: Then the maiden ran, and told in her mother's household all these things.
translations.29: And Rebekah had a brother, whose name was Laban; and Laban ran out to the man, outside, to the spring.
translations.30: And when he saw the nose-ring, and the bracelets upon his sister's hands, and heard her words, saying: 'Thus did the man say to me' — he went out to him; and behold, he was standing by the camels at the spring.
translations.31: And he said: 'Come in, O blessed of God! Why do you stand outside? I have already cleared the house, and prepared a place for the camels.'
translations.32: And the man came into the house; and he unloaded the camels; and he gave straw and feed to the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the feet of the men who were with him.
translations.33: Then [food] was set before him to eat. But he said: 'I will not eat until I have said my words.' He said: 'Speak.'
translations.34: He said: 'I am the servant of Abraham.
translations.35: And God has greatly blessed my master, and he has grown great. And He has given him sheep and cattle, and silver and gold, and male and female slaves, and camels and donkeys.
translations.36: And Sarah, my master's wife, bore him a son in her old age; and he gave to him all that he has.
translations.37: And my master made me swear, saying: "You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites in whose land I dwell;
translations.38: rather to my father's house you shall go, and to my kindred; and you shall take a wife for my son."
translations.39: And I said to my master: 'Perhaps the woman will not follow me.'
translations.40: And he said to me: 'God, in whose obedience I have walked, shall send His angel before you, and grant your way success; and you shall take a wife for my son from my kindred and from my father's house.
translations.41: Then shall you be free from this my charge — when you have come to my kindred. And if they shall not give her to you, you shall be free from my charge.'
translations.42: And I came today to the spring, and I said: 'O God, God of my master Abraham — if You are making my way prosper, on which I am going,
translations.43: behold, I am standing by the spring of water; let it be that the maiden who comes forth to draw, to whom I say, "Let me drink a little water from your jar,"
translations.44: and she says to me, "Drink, and I shall also water your camels" — she is the woman whom God has destined for the son of my master.'
translations.45: And before I had finished my speech in my heart — behold, Rebekah came forth, and her jar upon her shoulder; and she went down to the spring, and drew. And I said to her: 'Let me drink, now.'
translations.46: And she hastened, and let down her jar from her, and said: 'Drink, and I shall also water your camels.' And I drank, and she watered the camels.
translations.47: And I asked her, and said to her: 'Whose daughter are you?' She said: 'The daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, whom Milkah bore to him.' And I set the nose-ring upon her nose, and the bracelets upon her hands.
translations.48: And I bowed down and prostrated myself before God; and I blessed God, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me on a straight path, to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.
translations.49: And now — if you are doing kindness and grace with my master, tell me; and if not — tell me, that I may turn to the right or to the left.'
translations.50: And Laban and Bethuel answered, and said: 'From before God has this matter come forth; we cannot speak to you of evil or of good.
translations.51: Behold, Rebekah is before you. Take her and go; and let her be a wife for the son of your master, as God has destined.'
translations.52: And when Abraham's servant heard their words, he bowed down upon the earth before God.
translations.53: And the servant brought out vessels of silver and vessels of gold, and garments, and gave them to Rebekah; and her fruits he gave to her brother and her mother.
translations.54: And they ate and drank — he and the men who were with him — and they lodged. And when they rose in the morning, he said: 'Send me away to my master.'
translations.55: Her brother and her mother said: 'Let the maiden stay with us a year or ten [days]; and after that she may go.'
translations.56: He said to them: 'Delay me not, for God has made my way prosper. Send me away, that I may go to my master.'
translations.57: They said: 'Let us call the maiden, and inquire of her own words.'
translations.58: And they called Rebekah, and said to her: 'Will you go with this man?' And she said: 'Yes.'
translations.59: And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant, and his men.
translations.60: And they blessed Rebekah, and said to her: 'O our sister! May there come from you thousands and tens of thousands; and may your offspring possess the towns of those who hate them.'
translations.61: And Rebekah and her maidens arose, and rode upon the camels, and went with the man. And the servant took Rebekah, and went.
translations.62: And Isaac had come, on his way, from the Well of the Living One who Sees; and he was dwelling in the land of the qibla (the south).
translations.63: And Isaac went out, to pray in the wilderness toward the turning of evening; and he lifted up his eyes, and looked — and behold, camels approaching.
translations.64: And when Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and saw Isaac, she nearly fell from the camel.
translations.65: And she said to the servant: 'Who is this man going in the wilderness to meet us?' The servant said: 'He is my master.' And she took the veil, and covered herself with it.
translations.66: And the servant told Isaac all the things which he had done.
translations.67: And Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother; and he took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her. And Isaac was comforted concerning his mother.
